external_articles.title: Nvidia’s Hyperscaler Revenue Could Reach $401B In 2027, Says Analyst: SpaceX Could Push Barclays’ ‘Napkin Math’ Higher
external_articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) could end up generating more hyperscaler revenue than Wall Street currently expects, with Barclays analyst Tom O’Malley using “napkin math” from Nvidia’s latest IT spending data to estimate $401 billion in 2027 revenue.

In a note to investors cited by TheFly, he said the calculation leaves out SpaceX (SPCX) from the capex comparison, potentially making the implied revenue opportunity even larger.

NVDA stock edged 0.6% higher in morning trade on Thursday, with retail sentiment around the company on Stocktwits trending in ‘neutral’ territory over the past day.

According to O’Malley’s calculations, Nvidia could generate $237 billion in hyperscaler revenue in 2026 and $401 billion in 2027, compared with Barclays’ existing estimates of $206 billion and $370 billion, respectively.

In an upside scenario, the firm sees hyperscaler revenue reaching $246 billion in 2026 and $417 billion in 2027.

The calculation is based on a chart Nvidia shared, showing its share of IT capital spending among the five largest cloud service providers over the past several years, as well as its estimate for 2027. Nvidia’s share is projected to reach 44% in 2027, according to O’Malley.

Nvidia’s reported hyperscaler revenue includes SpaceX (SPCX), while the 44% IT capex share shown in its chart covers only the top five cloud service providers.

Barclays says that difference would imply an even larger total hyperscaler revenue figure if SpaceX were included in the spending-share calculation.

This matters because Nvidia’s AI infrastructure customer base has expanded beyond the traditional group of hyperscalers, with diversified companies spending heavily on GPUs and related infrastructure to build capacity for both AI training and inference.

The firm currently has an ‘Overweight’ rating on Nvidia with a $275 price target.

items.body: Bloomberg: Saudis Cut Flagship Oil Price to Asia to Lowest in Six Years This was what I meant when I said crude oil prices are going to fall Global crude demand/supply roughly balanced this past month (Sep) Refining capacities are somewhat stretched in the West and the Middle East (due to capacities being knocked offline) but I learnt last week that China is running at 70-80% utilization amongst the large SOEs, while the teapots are at around 50% But the reality is - domestic oil demand in China is in a structural decline, driven by electrification/cleaner transport. High oil prices are also a catalyst behind the shift EVs alone displaced 36 million tons of oil demand in 1H this year, 1/3 of overall decline in oil demand. Electric trucks had also emerged as the fastest-growing source of oil displacement, ​with alternative fuel use jumping 90% over the same period In fact, China has a massive crude stockpile (estimated to be 1.4 billion bbls) The only reason I can think of why they are still importing crude is to keep their refiners running without depleting their own strategic reserves, and to capture the spread/value from re-exports/distillates. They probably also see themselves swing trading as a way of wielding influence in the region

items.title: Aletheia Capital estimates that PCB content per Google $GOOGL TPU v8 rack could reach $30,000 to $40,000, up from about $20,000 for TPU v7. Its estimate assumes eight compute trays
items.body: Aletheia Capital estimates that PCB content per Google $GOOGL TPU v8 rack could reach $30,000 to $40,000, up from about $20,000 for TPU v7. Its estimate assumes eight compute trays per v8 rack, each with four TPUs. The firm expects CCL content per rack to rise to between $12,000 and $18,000, from about $7,000. It sees a further 40% to 50% increase in content per rack with TPU v9 as boards move to HDI. Aletheia’s supply-chain checks also point to more discussions between cloud providers and PCB and CCL suppliers about long-term agreements and prepayments to secure high-end capacity. Most of those talks are still ongoing. In networking, the firm expects PCB prices to rise from between $350 and $400 for 400G switches to about $1,500 for 800G models. For 1.6T, it sees prices reaching $3,000 to $4,000 as boards move to 44 to 50 layers and M9 laminates.
